title: What Is a Moat in Business? Explained Simply
chapters: Why does a business need a moat?
What is a moat made of?
What other kinds of moat are there?
How do you spot a fake moat?
Can one star person be a moat?
How do you test any business?

beats.say: Why does nobody ever copy Meena's sweet shop? Because it has a moat: something that keeps rivals out. This street is made up, but the idea is real. Raju's juice cart sold one thousand rupees a day. Then three copies opened right next to it. Now it sells two hundred and fifty. Raju needs a moat, fast.

beats.say: A moat can be made of very low costs, or of a famous brand known all over the world. Those are Buffett's two examples. Raju starts with low costs.
beats.cap: A moat can be made of very low costs, or of a famous brand known all over the world. Those are Buffett's two examples. Raju starts with low costs.

or of a famous brand known all over the world.
Those are Buffett's two examples.
Raju starts with low costs.

beats.say: Buffett wrote about GEICO, an American car insurer. Picture every hundred rupees that customers paid GEICO for car insurance in nineteen eighty six. Only twenty three rupees and fifty paise went on running costs. Many big rivals spent about fifteen rupees more.
beats.cap: Buffett wrote about GEICO, an American car insurer. Picture every ₹100 that customers paid GEICO for car insurance in 1986. Only ₹23.50 went on running costs. Many big rivals spent about ₹15 more (about ₹38.50, our arithmetic).

Picture every ₹100 that customers paid GEICO for car insurance in 1986.
Only ₹23.50 went on running costs.
Many big rivals spent about ₹15 more (about ₹38.50, our arithmetic).

beats.say: Our reading is that costs that low let GEICO charge less, or keep more. Buffett called that gap a kind of moat.
beats.cap: Our reading is that costs that low let GEICO charge less, or keep more. Buffett called that gap a kind of moat.
cues: Our reading is that costs that low let GEICO charge less, or keep more.
Buffett called that gap a kind of moat.

beats.say: He first learned about GEICO in nineteen fifty one. In his twenty thirteen letter, the low costs were still there. That is more than sixty years. Did any rival ever cross that moat? Buffett wrote that rivals were unable to cross it.
beats.cap: He first learned about GEICO in 1951. In his 2013 letter, the low costs were still there. That is more than 60 years. Did any rival ever cross that moat? Buffett wrote that rivals were unable to cross it.

beats.say: So Raju tries low costs. But all four carts buy cane from the same farm, at the same price. Nobody on the street can be much cheaper. A cost that everyone shares is not a moat.

beats.say: The second kind is a famous brand. In his nineteen ninety three letter, Buffett pointed to Coca Cola and Gillette. Out of every hundred soft drinks in the world, about forty four were Coke. Of all the money spent on razor blades, Gillette got more than sixty in every hundred. Why does a famous name keep rivals out?

beats.say: Famous names, good products, and wide sales. Together, he wrote, these set up a protective moat.
beats.cap: Famous names, good products, and wide sales. Together, he wrote, these set up a protective moat.

beats.say: First, the lock. Think of a salary account. Rent, loan payment and light bill all come out of it. A new account is easy to open. Moving every bill is the pain. Raju's cart has no lock. To leave him, a customer just walks to the next cart.

beats.say: Buffett has a line for this. A moat that must be continuously rebuilt will eventually be no moat at all. In plain words: if you must keep rebuilding it, it is not a moat. Four machines later, Raju is back where he started.

Of every hundred rupees customers paid, twenty four rupees and ten paise went on running costs. A year later, twenty three rupees and fifty paise. Sixty paise saved on every hundred rupees, in one year.

beats.say: Quick recap. A moat keeps rivals out. A business needs one because rivals attack whoever earns well. It can be made of low costs, a brand, a lock, a crowd or a licence. A fake moat is soon crossed, or must be rebuilt again and again. One star is not a moat. No moat lasts forever. And the test? Copy, rebuild, one person.
